question: Does a complete session produce what IDC-AC-7 asks for, and does the reader read it honestly?

setup.daemon: rebuilt from main at #1529, re-signed with the maintainer's Developer ID; previous bundle kept under Helpers/.backup-20260826T104711/
setup.device: DAYU200 development board, target TGT-958780b2ffb7 binding r4
setup.request: capture.diagnostics@1, ringBuffered, ohos+graphic at 20480 KiB, hilog, crash log, screenshot, two manual marks

produced.privacy: hilog, crash index, crash log, screenshot and trace are sensitive; capture log, markers, index and summary are standard

marks.automaticTrigger: crashLogCaptured, from a crash log that really arrived (395942 bytes, from com.example.lazydemo on the device)

whatTheReaderSaid: alignment: cannotAlign - no host-to-device calibration was established, which is the honest state and the default
mark 1 'session start': the nearest screenshot was +16000 ms away, so no picture stands for it
mark 2 'stutter here': the nearest screenshot was -6000 ms away, so no picture stands for it
mark 3 (automatic, crashLogCaptured): no screenshot was taken at it
notDerived carried through: frameDeadline and logKeyword

gapFound.what: the applies-to-this-mark case could not be demonstrated, and not because the marks were badly aimed
detail: The rule the design sets is that a screenshot stands for a mark when the shutter
opened within 150 ms of it. What the runtime records is the artifact's
Two things follow. The recorded instant is when the artifact was written, not
when the shutter opened; and its granularity is about seven times coarser than
the window that consumes it. No aim, however careful, can put a mark inside a
150 ms window measured against a value rounded to the second.
The reader is not wrong here - it refused correctly, and said by how much. The
fact it needs is not published yet.
whatWouldCloseIt: The screenshot leg records the instant its own readback observed, at millisecond
resolution, as a fact on the artifact - the design's `截图 Artifact 记录实际拍摄时刻`
read literally. Until then the ±150 ms rule is written and tested but cannot fire
on real data, and this file is the place that says so.
gapFound.supersededBy: shutter-instant.json. The granularity described here was the symptom. With the instant recorded at millisecond resolution the rule still cannot be met: the capture itself is ~930 ms wide, so the host cannot locate the shutter to ±150 ms no matter how precise its clock is.

IDC-AC-7: Met: a session with manual and automatic marks produced markers.json, a
retrospective trace whose reach is provable from its own anchor, hilog, a crash
log and a screenshot; every artifact passed status, privacy, byte and SHA checks;
the reader lines up only on time facts, shows the two-state alignment, and
degrades honestly when it cannot align or cannot find a picture.
Not met: the `+N ms` label on an applying screenshot. It is implemented and
tested, and cannot be exercised end to end until the shutter instant is recorded
